### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in settleBulkStoredExpressions))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 045dae8f23d21e7631e425bb851cad5ab2bc26fd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78a567b29c467179c2960e187c8d189e99db5df8` — the merge of head `c22a069d3dbc63130ecf78b590d5550ee2677d96` into base `045dae8f23d21e7631e425bb851cad5ab2bc26fd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78a567b29c467179c2960e187c8d189e99db5df8 && git checkout 78a567b29c467179c2960e187c8d189e99db5df8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 045dae8f23d21e7631e425bb851cad5ab2bc26fd c22a069d3dbc63130ecf78b590d5550ee2677d96 && git checkout -B drift-repro 045dae8f23d21e7631e425bb851cad5ab2bc26fd && git merge --no-ff c22a069d3dbc63130ecf78b590d5550ee2677d96

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 045dae8f23d21e7631e425bb851cad5ab2bc26fd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 045dae8f23d21e7631e425bb851cad5ab2bc26fd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c01e0622788ed39c9ac8a49096a75ceee102bc2e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-stored-expression-write.test.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts, examples/app-crm/src/objects/opportunity-line-item.object.ts + .changeset/24619-stored-expression-computed-on-write.md and content/docs/references/data/field.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx, content/docs/references/system/migration.mdx (the prose faces, read sentence by sentence), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`stripReadonlyFields`, `stripReadonlyWhenFields`, `stripReadonlyWhenFieldsMulti`, `needsPriorRecord`, `hasParentScopedRequiredWhen`), packages/objectql/src/hook-write-provenance.ts (`recordHookPayloadWrites`, the `set` trap), packages/objectql/src/index.ts and packages/objectql/src/core.ts (unchanged at this head), packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts (`writeRecord`, `decideWriteAction`, `isNoOpReplay`, `SEED_OPTIONS`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`updateManyData`, `runUpdateManyLoop`, the data doors' `engine.insert` / `engine.update` calls), packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts (the `/batch` update and the `updateMany` route), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts (`update_record`), packages/plugins/organizations/src/claim-org-seed-ownership.ts (the one `multi: true` writer), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`update` by id), packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (`judgeFieldFormula`), packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts (`EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema`), examples/app-showcase/src/data/seed/index.ts (the five `showcase_invoice_line` rows), content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx and content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx (hand-written, unchanged), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the narrowing arm), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`no-migration-prescription`), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (the Check Changeset job), AGENTS.md (the trailer pair, the changeset rule, the regenerate-and-commit rule), .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, lanes/spec.md, app-platform-boundary.md, filing-gate.md, SKILL.md (the four axes, the domain path table). Inputs: card #24619's body and all five comments (triage 6272616654, claim 6277262398, dispatch 6277306080, routing 6278345889, the `os-dev-report` 6278955805 read as claims); #4889 with both comments; the PR body and file list (9 files, +498/-38, matching `git diff` against the merge base `cc95f5e63e3c96acafa55378a57d06c086e7d639`); the head's check-runs, read twice.

### ① Derived judgments

**The computation point: two passes on insert and by-id update, one on predicate update.**
- *Insert* (`engine.insert`, the batch and `insertMany` doors): `planStoredExpressions` runs once per call; pass 1 computes over `defaultedData` (after `applyFieldDefaults` and `initializeSummaryFields`, so `quantity`'s default 1 is read) BEFORE the hook-write recording is armed and before `beforeInsert`; pass 2 computes over the final rows after the hooks, `stripRuntimeOwnedFields`, the static `readonly` strip and the post-image seam, immediately before `normalizeMultiValueFields` and `validateRecordInScope`, so the stored value is validated. Right.
- *Update by id*: pass 1 computes over `{ ...priorRecord, ...patch }` after the prior-row read and before `beforeUpdate`; pass 2 computes over `{ ...priorRecord, ...finalPatch }` after `stripReadonlyWhenFields`, `stripReadonlyFields` and `assertNoStrictDrops()`, before the post-image seam, `evaluateValidationRules` and `driver.update`. Nothing between pass 2 and the statement writes a value, so the stored value is the expression over the stored row: a hook that sets the field is overwritten (pinned), a hook that moves an input is recomputed (pinned), a locked input the `readonlyWhen` strip took back out feeds the stored value (the card's `/batch` shape, pinned). Right.
- *Predicate update*: ONE pass, after both strips and `assertNoStrictDrops()`, through `settleBulkStoredExpressions`. The per-row `beforeUpdate` dispatch (`dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`) runs BEFORE it on the raw patch, so on this path the hooks are handed the CALLER's value (for example `amount: 1`), which the settle then deletes. The changeset's "The `before*` hooks are handed the computed value" is false on this path. Wrong as written; see ②.
- *What a `before*` hook sees on by-id is not always what is stored.* Pass 1 reads the pre-strip patch, so on the card's `/batch` write (`quantity: 60`, `amount: 2999.4` on a paid line) the hook is handed `quantity 60` and `amount 2999.4`, and the row stores `quantity 6`, `amount 299.94`. The locked input was already shown to hooks before this head (`readonlyWhen` is deliberately not hidden, engine.ts "⛔ `readonlyWhen` is NOT hidden and must not be", #9107), so the derived value shares a pre-existing exposure rather than opening one; but the code comment at the pass ("so a hook is handed the value the write stores (#16344's ruling)") and the dev report's reading of #16344 are false for exactly the card's case. Not a store-side defect; a wording and a citation to correct.
- *Field-level security, read-only strips, later steps*: the FLS write gate judges the caller's keys on `opCtx.data` at middleware time, never the engine-added key, so a caller editable on an input moves the derived column (right for a derived value) and a caller editable on the derived column alone cannot move it (overwritten from the stored inputs). The post-image RLS `check` seams on all three paths judge the final row with the computed value. `stripComputedWriteFields` still filters on `type === 'formula'` only, so a stored expression field is not stripped. No later step leaves a disagreeing value. Right.

**The pre-hook pass on by-id writes inside the hook-write recording window, and that moves an undeclared accept-set edge — WRONG.**
- `hookContext.input.data` is `hookWrites.payload`, the Proxy `recordHookPayloadWrites(opCtx.data)` returns (engine.ts, the `[#14088] ARM` block). Pass 1 does `applyStoredExpressionsToPatch(patch, computed, priorRecord)` on that Proxy, so every key it sets goes through the `set` trap (`hook-write-provenance.ts`: `Reflect.set` then `record(key)`) and lands in `hookWrittenKeys` as a HOOK write. The engine's own rule two screens up: "Placed BEFORE the recording is armed: a pass running inside that window is an ENGINE write recorded as a HOOK write, which is the laundering the seal note below exists to make impossible." The insert path obeys it (its pass 1 runs on `defaultedData` before `rowHookContexts` arm the recording); the by-id path does not.
- Consequence, on a shape `FieldSchema` admits and nothing refuses: a stored field declaring BOTH `readonly: true` AND `expression`. Before this head, a by-id update carrying the caller's value of that field had it hidden from the hooks, handed back, judged by `stripReadonlyFields` (`supplied` has it, `Object.is` holds), dropped with a `readonly` event through `onFieldsDropped`, and refused with `ReadonlyFieldRejectedError` under `strictReadonlyWrites`. At this head, when the same patch also moves an input, pass 1 re-adds the key with the computed value (not in the hidden patch; prior differs), the hand-back skips it (`k in target`), and the strip keeps it: `hookWrittenKeys.has(name)` is true, and even without the recorder the `Object.is` value test reads the engine's overwrite as "a hook overwrote this". No `readonly` event, no strict refusal, where both fired before. The stored value is still the computed one (pass 2), so the card's writes are unaffected.
- Reach: the census finds no in-tree stored expression field declaring `readonly`, and no in-repo producer passes `strictReadonlyWrites: true` (only the contract declarations and the error class name it). The accept/refuse behaviour of a published door is outside the in-repo radius, and the reading discipline says a missing victim is not evidence there. The changeset's "Unchanged" list does not name `readonly`, so this is an undeclared move on the narrowing face.
- Route (the seat's or the dev's choice, named here, not prescribed): keep the pre-hook image for the hooks but off the strips' payload, as the #16344 hide/hand-back pair already does for `readonly` values (compute onto the hook VIEW and let the strips judge the caller's submission); or skip, in pass 1 only, any stored expression field the caller supplied, letting pass 2 overwrite it (this gives up the "hook sees the computed value" pin for a caller-sent wrong value); either way write pass 1 outside the recording window, as the insert path does, and pin a `readonly` plus `expression` field on by-id update with `onFieldsDropped` and with `strictReadonlyWrites`.

**On update, the merged row is a read the write already makes; the cost and the authority.** `priorRecord` is read unconditionally on every by-id update since #7867 (`readUpdatePriorRow`: a raw `driver.findOne` by id under `buildDriverOptions` — tenant scope and the open transaction — shaped to declared columns), so pass 1 and pass 2 add no read; they add two evaluations per stored field and two `resolveFormulaRelated` calls that return without a query when the expression traverses nothing (both examples read own columns only). The image is the raw stored row, not the caller's served image: columns field-level security would hide from the caller still feed the expression, which is right for a column that already derives from them. On the predicate path the rows come from `readPriorRows`, a memo over `driver.find(object, ast)` on the middleware-composed AST (RLS and sharing scoped). The dev's "no second read" is true; "a read the write already makes" holds only when per-row hooks exist (`hasHooksFor`), `needsPriorRecord` holds, the payload carries a `readonlyWhen` field, or a post-image check is installed. On a bare `@objectstack/objectql/core` embedder with an object declaring a stored expression and none of those, this head adds a FIRST read of the whole matched set, with no D6 ceiling (`assertBulkPerRowHookBudget` runs only when hooks exist). In a composed kernel the global `afterUpdate` registrants already force the read. Cost note, not blocking.

**Overwrite, in every context.** `planStoredExpressions` has no `isSystem` gate, so the overwrite reaches the console grid (sends the computed value; stored as sent — pinned), forms and read-modify-write (echo the stored value; stored as sent), MCP (`mcp-http-tools.ts` `update` is by id), imports and `/batch` (`batch-routes.ts` calls `ql.update(object, { ...data, id })`), the REST `updateMany` door (`protocol.updateManyData` loops `runUpdateManyLoop` per record by id) and system writers. The seed loader writes under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` (`isSystem: true`): on insert the engine overwrites the seed's `amount` with the same value; on replay `isNoOpReplay` compares each seed key with the stored row and skips. The five seeded `showcase_invoice_line` rows satisfy `amount == quantity * unit_price` in IEEE-754 doubles (10 × 150, 4 × 29.99 = 119.96, 2 × 99, 6 × 49.99 = 299.94, 3 × 150 — the two inexact products are exactly the seeded literals), so every replay still no-ops and every invoice `total` is unchanged. The CRM seeds no line items. No in-repo writer stores a value its expression does not compute: the census (two stored fields) matches my own `expression` grep over `examples/**/*.object.ts`. One observation: the overwrite is silent to every `onFieldsDropped` consumer (automation `update_record` step warnings, `/batch` `droppedFields`, the PATCH door's `droppedFields`) — a flow that writes `amount: 1` reports success while the row holds 299.94, the shape #3407 ruled must be reported for the strips. Reporting it would need a new `DroppedFieldsEvent.reason` (the `computed` reason is contracted as "dropped, and the write completed without them", and this key IS written), which is a spec widening; flagged in ③, not blocking.

**The predicate-update refusal.** `settleBulkStoredExpressions` deletes the field from the patch, then: no row's computed value moves ⇒ column untouched (the caller's value is dropped); every row moves to one value ⇒ that value is set once on the patch, so ONE `updateMany` statement stores it; otherwise `ValidationError([{ field, code: 'invalid_value', message }])` is thrown before `driver.updateMany`, so nothing is written. `VALIDATION_FAILED` and `invalid_value` are existing codes. In-repo reachability: `service-automation`'s `update_record` node forwards `where: filter, multi: cfg.multi === true` to `data.update`, so a flow with `multi: true` and a filter over lines with differing `unit_price` setting `quantity` is refused and the step returns `success: false` with the message naming the by-id remedy; `claim-org-seed-ownership` (`multi: true`) moves no input, so its patch is untouched. `/batch`, the REST `updateMany` door and MCP are by id and never reach it. "Moves no input" is judged on COMPUTED values before and after, not on the stored column, so a legacy row whose column disagrees with its expression keeps the stale value through a predicate update that moves no input, while a by-id update of any key corrects it (`applyStoredExpressionsToPatch` adds the key when `prior` differs). Right, with the stale-row nuance noted against the ADR-0087 marker's "keeps it until the row is next written" in ②.

**Null on fault.** `applyFormulaPlan` answers `null` and calls the sink once per (object, field) per engine instance (`reportFormulaFault`). So an insert of a line with `quantity` but no `unit_price` now stores `amount: null` where it stored the caller's value or nothing; the dogfood persona insert the dev names stored absent before and `null` now, the same read. The `min: 0` on `amount` does not judge `null`. No seed loses a number (all five lines carry both inputs; CRM seeds none), and `sum` skips `null`. "A declared expression is enforced" read as "the column holds the expression's answer, `null` included" is the formula read path's semantic and is right for a derived column; the log line still says "reads null" for a column that now STORES null (open question 5).

**The paid-line pins.** `engine-stored-expression-write.test.ts` drives the real `ObjectQL` over a driver whose `find` honours `limit`, with the showcase shape trimmed and the header rows present, so the parent-scoped `readonlyWhen` resolves through `resolveMasterDetailParent`. The `/batch`-shaped pin asserts `quantity 6`, `amount 299.94`, the drop set exactly `[quantity] readonly_when`; the amount-only PATCH pin asserts `299.94`. Both have teeth: with the planner guard ablated the stored `amount` is `2999.4` and `1`. The invoice `total` in the suite is the test's own sum over the store, not the engine's `summary` recompute (`showcase_invoice` is registered without a `total` field), so "total unchanged" is pinned by proxy; the real roll-up follows the stored column through `recomputeSummaries`. The draft control (consistent grid save stored as sent) is right. The CRM `line_total` is not pinned; the dev's booted-CRM table is a claim, and the code path is the showcase's minus the strips. By my reading of the twelve cases against an empty plan, ten go red (the two paid-line writes, no-amount update, wrong-amount update, the insert trio, the batch insert, the hook case, and all three predicate cases) and two stay green (the consistent save; the no-input patch whose stored 30 equals the pre-state), matching the dev's 10/2.

**No public surface moves.** `formulaPlanEntry`, `planStoredExpressions`, `computeStoredExpressions`, `settleBulkStoredExpressions`, `applyStoredExpressionsToPatch` are module-level `function`s and `StoredExpressionServing` a module-level `interface`, none exported; the only new import is the existing `FieldValidationError` type. `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `core.ts` and `package.json` are byte-identical to the merge base; no new member on `ObjectQL` (both hunks are inside `insert` and `update`). Consistent with this lane's rulings on PRs #24518 and #24526. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql`: `minor` with the BREAKING banner and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at a line start in the changeset and on line 3 of the PR body. Right: the write doors' accept set narrows (a client value no longer stands; one predicate shape is refused), no key, value, export or code is added, and `check-changeset-no-major` reads the arm as "a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`" (its self-test: a declared narrowing graded `minor` is clean). The Check Changeset run on this head is green, so the gate read it.
- `@objectstack/spec`: the package's own diff is describe and TSDoc only; the schema's accept set is byte-identical, which lanes/spec.md calls the auxiliary face (normally `patch`). It rides the one narrowing changeset, whose arm asks `minor` of the bumped packages, so `minor` is gate-consistent; the alternative is a separate `patch` changeset for the describe. Acceptable as committed.
- Narrowing or widening of meaning? No new accepted key or value: `expression` was already optional on every field type, the lint already judged it on any field (`judgeFieldFormula` reads `f.expression` regardless of `type`), and the console grid already consumed it on stored fields. The describe now states the server meaning of a key the server ignored: the spec lane's "declared ≠ enforced" face (lanes/spec.md lists it among the five contract shapes, and says a narrowing does not trigger Clause-②). So `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` stands, the published schema face is hit, and the spec lane's review applies — served by this record at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, with the cross-seat declaration still owed (③).
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the category exists in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`; its mechanical check (the body carries no migration prescription) and the "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset" step inside Check Changeset are green on this head. The Fix line is a behavioural prescription, not a metadata rewrite — no key moves and `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to do — so the category is the right one of the set. One sentence in the marker overstates: "A stored row whose value disagrees with its expression keeps it until the row is next written" — a predicate update that moves no input is a write that leaves it stale (①).
- FROM: true. TO: "computes after the `before*` hooks and both read-only strips" true (pass 2); "The `before*` hooks are handed the computed value" false on the predicate path and, on by-id, a value that is not the stored one whenever a locked input is in the patch (①) — rewrite it as "on insert and update by id, the `before*` hooks are handed the expression over the pre-strip row; a predicate update's per-row hooks are handed the caller's patch"; "A caller's value is overwritten, in every context" true; "A patch that moves none of the expression's inputs stores the value the row already computes to" true by id, qualified for the predicate path by the Refused bullet; the `null`-on-fault sentence true (sink once per object and field per engine instance); the summary sentence true. Refused: true sentence by sentence (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, `invalid_value`, before anything is written, one value stored once, no-input leaves the column alone). Unchanged: true for `formula`, for fields without `expression` and for a client sending the computed value; it omits the `readonly` plus `expression` shape ① finds moved. Fix: true, and "remove the field's `expression`" also removes the grid's read-only cell, which the sentence does not say.
- The spec describe: "computed by the engine on every insert and update from the row the write stores ... and stored, so a client-sent value never stands" — "never stands" is true on every path (overwritten, dropped or refused); "on every ... update ... and stored" overstates the predicate path (left alone when no input moves; refused when values differ). Tighten in the same round.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 (`content/docs/references/**`, three generated files outside the claim's fence):** accepted. AGENTS.md "Touched `packages/spec`? Regenerate and commit its artifacts before pushing" makes it required; lanes/spec.md says the regenerated references belong to the source PR; the three mdx rows carry the describe byte for byte, and no "Formula expression (CEL)" remains anywhere at this head.
- **Deviation 2 (commit trailers):** not a deviation under this repo's rule. AGENTS.md: "an agent commit ends with the model-free trailer pair `Claude-Session` ... and `Co-authored-by: Claude`, and the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier in that pair"; the six authored commits carry exactly that pair, the merge commit none. Accepted, as on PR #24526.
- **Deviation 3 (shape A not taken; CRM metadata untouched):** within the claim's "by the shape the measurement picks" and the dispatch's "shape A or shape B". Accepted. The showcase comment's "with no `readonlyWhen` of its own" is true for updates; the insert exemption is finding 1 below.
- **Open questions, by the four axes (SKILL.md: actual business need; long-term soundness at or above half the weight; preventing AI authoring errors; startup-stage scope):**
  1. *B over A:* accepted. Two measured defects and only B closes the API/MCP one; B is the SKILL's own ruling principle ("a declaration not honoured is an implementation gap: implement or retire, never narrow at the consumer"); declared becomes enforced; no new key or code.
  2. *Overwrite, not refuse:* accepted on the first two axes (whole-record round-trips would 400). On the third axis it is weaker than the dev says: an agent that sends a wrong value learns nothing, because the overwrite reports through no channel (①).
